definition: In an unwilling, resentful way, as when doing something you would rather not do.
example: He begrudgingly admitted that his little sister's plan was better than his own.
nuance: Begrudgingly adds a note of resentment that reluctantly lacks; you give in, but you are not happy about it.
prompt: A teenager is told to clean out the garage on a sunny Saturday.
options: Sighing loudly, she begrudgingly dragged the old boxes to the curb.
She begrudgingly volunteered, thrilled to finally have a chance to tidy up.
She begrudgingly skipped the chore entirely and spent the day at the pool.
She begrudgingly agreed to the job, though no one had asked her to do anything.
reasons: She does the chore but makes her resentment plain, which is exactly the right tone.
Being thrilled contradicts the resentment and reluctance the word requires.
The word describes giving in unwillingly, not avoiding the task altogether.
Reluctant compliance needs some pressure or request to resent; here there is none.

practice.prompt: A chess player loses a close match to a much younger opponent.
options: He begrudgingly shook her hand and admitted she had played the better game.
He begrudgingly congratulated her, beaming with pure, wholehearted delight at her win.
He begrudgingly refused to shake her hand and stormed out of the room.
His begrudgingly was obvious to everyone still watching the board.
reasons: He concedes defeat even though it stings, showing unwilling but real acceptance.
Wholehearted delight leaves no room for the resentment the word implies.
Refusing outright is not yielding; the word marks something done despite unwillingness.
An adverb cannot act as a noun here; a word like reluctance would be needed.
